doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Cat Anderson and the borrowed money
summary: Young tells how Cat Anderson borrowed gambling money and refused to repay him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I worked with Cat in a band, me and Cat was gambling, Cat lost all his money so he said, ―Hey Snooky, let me have some money.‖ I said, ―Ok.‖ I think I gave him ten or fifteen dollars, something like that. I asked him for my money and he say, ―You better get out of here, get away from me.‖ I asked him for it a couple days later, I say, ―Give me my money, I get [inaudible] money, you better get out of here, I ain‘t thinking about you.‖ That‘s what he did, that‘s the kind of cat he was, Cat was strange, man. But he never got no more money from me. [laughs] He never got no more money from me, man. He was strange, man.
